[[File:Young Jedi Darth Maul Sith Apprentice.gif|thumb|right|200px|''Darth Maul, Sith Apprentice'' (''Menace of Darth Maul'', 1999).]]
'''Young Jedi''' is Decipher's 1999 ''Star Wars'' customizable card game based on ''The Phantom Menace''. It is a different game from [[Star Wars CCG]]. Decipher held both licenses; designers, Squadron Members, and the player base overlapped.

The [[Corellian Engineering Corporation (fan site)|Corellian Engineering Corporation]] GeoCities site published two Young Jedi lists next to its Classic Star Wars decks. The lists, ''Wizards!'' (Jedi) and ''All Droids All the time!'' (Sith), were both by Gold 31 ([[Alex Alcalde]]). Archived copies: [https://www.geocities.ws/plarathas/decks/jedi1.html jedi1.html] · [https://web.archive.org/web/20011202101302/http://www.geocities.com/CollegePark/Plaza/9433/decks/jedi1.html Wayback, 2 December 2001]; [https://www.geocities.ws/plarathas/decks/sith1.html sith1.html] · [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009020148/https://www.geocities.ws/plarathas/decks/sith1.html Wayback, 9 October 2026].

== Design ==
''Young Jedi'' was designed by [[Tom Braunlich]] and [[Rollie Tesh]], with [[Bill Martinson]] and [[Jerry Darcy]] developing it further. Decipher aimed it at 9- to 13-year-olds, and Braunlich said he had hoped for a simpler game with broader appeal than SWCCG. It kept SWCCG's destiny numbers, locations and Force depletion as the goal of the game.<ref name="rfd16">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yy8IGS_I1UI&t=100s Broadcast 16 - Radio Free Decipher (30 April, 1999): Rollie Tesh, Tom Braunlich (Part 2)], Player's Council, YouTube (uploaded 20 February 2022), at 01:40. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-yy8IGS_I1UI Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Episode 16 transcript]].</ref><ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yy8IGS_I1UI&t=205s Broadcast 16 - Radio Free Decipher (30 April, 1999): Rollie Tesh, Tom Braunlich (Part 2)], Player's Council, YouTube (uploaded 20 February 2022), at 03:25. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-yy8IGS_I1UI Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Episode 16 transcript]].</ref> In April 1999 Decipher's [[Carol Wisely]] noted that ''Young Jedi'' was the company's first game with numbered cards and rarity icons, and that its first set had 140 cards, against 324 in SWCCG's Premiere.<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yy8IGS_I1UI&t=425s Broadcast 16 - Radio Free Decipher (30 April, 1999): Rollie Tesh, Tom Braunlich (Part 2)], Player's Council, YouTube (uploaded 20 February 2022), at 07:05. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-yy8IGS_I1UI Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Episode 16 transcript]].</ref>

== Sets ==
Decipher released eight Young Jedi sets between May 1999 and September 2001: ''Menace of Darth Maul'', ''The Jedi Council'', ''Battle of Naboo'', ''Enhanced Menace of Darth Maul'', ''Duel of the Fates'', ''Enhanced Battle of Naboo'', ''Young Jedi Reflections'' and ''Boonta Eve Podrace''.<ref name="cl">[http://www.decipher.com/youngjedi/cardlists/index.html Young Jedi Card Lists], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20021201080954/http://www.decipher.com/youngjedi/cardlists/index.html Internet Archive]</ref>

== Organized play ==
The first Young Jedi World Championship was held at DecipherCon 1999, with 32 players advancing from four Friday qualifiers. Decipher wrote that "most have some Star Wars CCG experience". Greg Heisler won, and Matt Reed was runner-up.<ref name="wc99">[http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/yjworldchamp/index.html DecipherCon 1999: Young Jedi World Championship], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20000124144623/http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/yjworldchamp/index.html Internet Archive]</ref> The 2000 Young Jedi World Championship, won by Ian Vincent, ran at [[DecipherCon 2000]] alongside the SWCCG World Championship.<ref name="dc00">[http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/ DecipherCon 2000], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040217015645/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/ Internet Archive]</ref>

== Design (1999 interviews) ==
Decipher product development leads [[Jerry Darcy]] and [[Bill Martinson]] discussed the game on ''[[Radio Free Decipher]]'' in April 1999, about five weeks before release. Darcy described it as a quicker "pickup game" than the ''Star Wars'' CCG. He said it could not be compatible with that game because ''Episode I'' lacked the Rebellion–Empire conflict and the same characters appear at very different ages.<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DsqnSbxT25c&t=771s Broadcast 12 - Radio Free Decipher (02 April, 1999): Bill Martinson, Jerry Darcy on PD (Part 1)], Player's Council, YouTube (uploaded 20 February 2022), at 12:51. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-DsqnSbxT25c Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Episode 12 transcript]].</ref> Martinson said the game was Warren Holland's conception, had been in development since October 1998, and was a focused battle game with a short turn sequence. He said it was planned as three 140-card sets, with a deck-building system proposed by Holland, and that a broad game could not be made before the film was released because the film's details were still changing.<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XvKFYzu0P-k&t=293s Broadcast 13 - Radio Free Decipher (09 April, 1999): Bill Martinson, Jerry Darcy on PD (Part 2)], Player's Council, YouTube (uploaded 20 February 2022), at 04:53. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-XvKFYzu0P-k Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Episode 13 transcript]].</ref>
